title: MV First dates (Visual Novel, including free VN plugin)

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
INTRO
First Dates is a visual Novel / Dating Sim. You are the main character, NPC's will interact with you, and you decide how you react to their dialogue.
I use RPG maker MV for the mechanics, and graphics from VN Maker. This because those graphics are really nice, but I simply know a lot more about RPG maker thank I know about VN maker. This does mean I have much freedom in how I make the scenes.
STORY
You are a student in high school. It is the end of the first day of the last week before summer break. You have a secret crush on one of your classmates, but he or she (your choice) has no idea. You have not spoken much and they barely even know you exist.
At the end of your last class your crush and their friend come over to ask if you would sign their yearbook. This is where you pick your crush. (Is it Willow, or Victor?)
How the story goes from here, all depends on the choices you make. From the very first word you speak to your crush, you start collection ♥. The more slick your reaction, the more ♥ you will earn, and the more romantic the story will be.
If you're rude to your crush, however, you will not gather any ♥ at all. This will soon translate in your crush not liking you at all, and the romantic story will shift to a more comedic story.
You will have your first interactions in and around your school, but will soon go trough the park, have some alone time at home before you meet your crush for a date at the fair. Where you go after this, all depends on how you behave on the first date.
(Post continues under the video)
GOAL
Well, the intended goal is to collect all the ♥ and get the ultimate romantic ending, with a fast-forward to the future, where you are happily married with children.
However, if you feel a bit more like a mean person today, you can try to get the ultimate bad ending. I won't spoil it all, but if you keep messing with your crush, you will get a whole different fast-forward.
And there will be a couple endings in between. All depending on how many stars you've collected along the way. Note that the difference in story doesn't start in the last scenes, though. If your first date went well, your second date will be in one place, while if it went horrible, your second date won't really be a date at all. That would meet for another reason in a different location.
FUN FACT
This game, so far, is completely evented in 1 single event. I only have 1 map with a size of 2x1, to put the player location and the event on. I can make the whole complete story with all alternative storylines in one single event page, but I will take a different page each time I make a split. This doesn't mean after every scene, since there are more scenes than splits in the story. (Even though without a hard split, your crush can still react differently if you have more or less ♥)
So, I will probably be able to make the whole game in a single event (all 20 pages), maybe 2.
Including Visual Novel Plugin for MV!!
How the picture move is done with rather large script-calls I wrote for this purpose. Now I am in the process to make this easier on myself by writing a plugin. This plugin will make the foreground character(s) and the background shift according to who the player is talking to. This is what the script calls now do as well, but this will be much easier with plugin commands.
The plugin works for up to 10 characters, but can easily be extended to a larger base. Files will need to be named a certain way:
Character need to be named in this format:
char_[name]_[outfit]_[mood].js
EXAMPLE:
char_Willow_schooluniform_happy.js
char_Victor_casual_angry.js
Locations need to be named in this format:
loc_[location]_[time].js
EXAMPLE:
loc_Classroom_morning.js
loc_Home_evening.js
The plugin will also include a character selections scene I made, which looks absolutely slick... You'll see up to 7 (out of 10) main characters of which the one in the middle is the selected one. By choosing Next or Previous, it will cycle trough all available characters.
NOTE: This character selection scene was made for a different game! Stats are not included in the plugin function.
I don't use it myself, though, because I realized the player character doesn't even need an image since you never see yourself anyway. This is a lot easier for the developer and for the player it is easier to imagine they are the main character.
However, I did make the character selection already, before I realized this, so I will include this into the plugin for those who want to use it anyway.
Once my own game is completed,
I will add this plugin to the project
, with permission to the end user to use this plugin! (Of course I will ask for credits in the terms of use)

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Many plugins? This is all one single plugin, containing a few plugin commands. Like
ShowA
ShowFocusA
UpdateA
UpdateFocusA
HideA
HideFocusA
(And all of those with B instead of A)
Those will show character A or character B in a left or right side of the screen, and when the focus is on A, A will move to the center, and B will move to the outer side of the frame.
All the user has to do, is put the name of the PNG file in a variable, before triggering the plugin commands, so the plugin knows which image to show.
(I've broken it up in 3 pieces: Name, Outfit and Mood, but that is optional, since not everyone would have characters in multiple outfits or with different emotes in the full-sized image. This optional feature would require files to be named in a certain format. Important to note.)
Making this with events it is very doable, just a loooooot more work than making the entire plugin.
I did all the math, the testing and the fine-tuning. (Well, by the time I share the plugin, I will have it all finetuned. The movement is still clumsy in the VN video. I already improved it a lot, but it can still be a lot more smooth.)
But the plugin isn't the main product, though. I actually made it for myself, to make this Visual Novel. But since I made it, and I've seen requests about it in the past, I thought it would be a nice  bonus. That is basically what it is: A bonus.
It is much like when you played those old school DOS games in the 90's, then after you were done playing them, you would open the files create your own levels, right? Have you ever done that? That is what I want with this plugin: People who play my VN and think: "Wow, I want to make a story like this too, but I don't have the time/skill/discipline to event all that myself."

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Haha, nooooo. This is 1 plugin, with different positions and movement for the images, but you put the image names in a variable, which you can change at any time of the game, to show different characters.
The character shown with ShowA, will show up at the left, and the one shown with ShowB show up to the right.
So I have codes for two characters in a single scene at the same time. But once one character leaves, you can just change the variable and summon a new character.
I won't make an editional code for each NPC in a VN
Only the character selection scene has a max of 10 characters for which made 1 code to circulate all of them. The plugin commands for that scene are simple:
StartActorSelection
NextActor
PreviousActor
EndActorSelection
The user would event it like this:
Code:
◆Plugin Command：StartActorSelection
◆Loop
  ◆Show Choices：Show next character                              , Play as \c[14]\p[1]\c[0], Show previous character (Window, Middle, #1, -)
  ：When Show next character                             
    ◆Plugin Command：NextActor
    ◆
  ：When Play as \c[14]\p[1]\c[0]
    ◆Break Loop
    ◆
  ：When Show previous character
    ◆Plugin Command：PreviousActor
    ◆
  ：End
  ◆
：Repeat Above
◆Plugin Command：EndActorSelection
And that is all they have to do.
For this function, the filenames, actor ID's and picture ID's are given in the plugin parameters.
EDIT:
Oh wait, I see what you mean now. I have way how 1 plugin command is used by all names already, with the outfits and moods as optional feature. This uses 3 vars times 2 characters (one on the left, one on the right)
So, I would call the image as gameVariables.value(X)+'_'+gameVariables.value(Y)+'_'+gameVariables.value(Z) for a filename, where:
- X = Id of variable with actor name
- Y = Id of variable with outfit
- Z = Id of variable with mood
So, the user needs to set name, outfit and mood at the start of the scene, then they can just change var Z to a new mood during dialogue, and call for an update.
